feedback.problem: An old wall clock loses $30$ seconds every week. What differential equation describes the rate of change of the difference $T$ (in seconds) between the actual time and the time shown on the clock?  Assume that the time $t$ is measured in weeks.
feedback.worked_solution:
If the difference between the actual time and the time shown on the clock is $T$ seconds, then the rate of the change of this difference is $\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in weeks.

Since the difference *increases* by $30$ seconds each week, the rate of change of the difference is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=30.
$$
